finding.claim: The /logo handler fetches an attacker-supplied URL. Its only check is a substring test for "example.io" on the raw string. The substring can sit in the path, query, fragment or userinfo of a URL that points anywhere. An attacker can therefore make the server request internal hosts such as cloud metadata at 169.254.169.254 or localhost services. The response body is copied back to the attacker, so this is full-read SSRF. The default http.Get client also follows redirects, so an allowed-looking host could redirect to an internal target.
finding.source: r.FormValue("logo") at main.go:31 (query or form parameter on GET/POST /logo)
finding.sink: http.Get(raw) at main.go:36, with the response body written to the client via io.Copy at main.go:38

trace.note: Only check: strings.Contains(raw, "example.io"). This is not a parsed host check and does not verify scheme, host, or resolved IP.
http.Get(raw) uses the default client, which follows redirects. The URL is passed unmodified.
The response body is returned to the attacker.

finding.guards_checked: The substring check on the raw string is the only guard. It is bypassable with, for example, http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/?x=example.io, http://127.0.0.1:8081/cdn#example.io, http://example.io@169.254.169.254/ or http://example.io.attacker.com/. There is no scheme check, no host allowlist, no resolved-IP check, and redirects are not disabled. The code has no egress filtering, and I did not review network-level egress.

verdict.guard_found: Only strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") at main.go:32 (a substring check, not a closing guard). No auth middleware is registered at main.go:43. The strict hostname allowlist and no-redirect client apply only to the separate /cdn handler (main.go:10-25), not to /logo.
verdict.reason: main.go:31 takes the URL from r.FormValue("logo"), main.go:32 only does a substring check that URLs like http://169.254.169.254/?x=example.io pass, and main.go:36 calls http.Get(raw) with the default redirect-following client and main.go:38 returns the body, so this is full-read SSRF.
